units.translation: b. Arcadians, who even before: The Arcadians are thought to have existed before the moon, as Eudoxus also says in his Circuit of the Earth (fr. 41 Brandes). Theodorus in his twenty-second book (62 fr. 2 J.) says that the moon appeared a little before Heracles' war against the Giants. And Aristias of Chios in his Foundations and Dionysius of Chalcis in the first book of his Foundations (fr. 1 M. IV 393) say that there is also a people of Arcadia called Selenitae. — Mnaseas (fr. 4 M. III 150) says that Proselenus ruled over the Arcadians. Aristotle in his Constitution of the Tegeans (fr. 549 Rose 1568b 41) says that barbarians inhabited Arcadia, who were expelled by the present Arcadians, who attacked them before the moon rose; for this reason they were called proselenoi. 〈...〉. Duris in the fifteenth book of his Macedonian History (76 fr. 9 J.) says that Arcas, from whom Arcadia is named, was the son of Orchomenus, and for this reason there is also a city of Arcadia called Orchomenus. Some say that Endymion discovered the circuits and numbers of the moon, whence the Arcadians were also called proselenoi. Others say that by Typhon 〈...〉; and by Atlas, as Xenagoras (240 fr. 32 J.) has said.

265-66. ruled over the Deucalionids: Those who trace their lineage from Deucalion ruled Thessaly, as Hecataeus (1 fr. 14 J.) and Hesiod (fr. 8 Rz.²) say. Thessaly was called Pelasgis after Pelasgus, who was its king.
